question: Which military operation was launched to integrate Hyderabad into India in 1948?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Operation Polo**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Operation Polo** was a military operation conducted by the **Indian Armed Forces** in **1948**.
 
• The operation was aimed at integrating the **Princely State of Hyderabad** into the **Indian Union**.
 
• The state of Hyderabad, under the rule of the **Nizam**, had refused to join India after independence in **1947**.
 
• It was a five-day operation conducted between **13th September and 17th September 1948**.
 
• The operation resulted in the defeat of the **Nizam's forces** and the annexation of Hyderabad into India.
 
• Major-General **J.N. Chaudhuri** led the Indian Army during this operation.
 
• The successful execution of Operation Polo marked the end of the Nizam's rule in Hyderabad.
 
• The operation was also referred to as the "**Police Action**" by the Government of India.
 
• Hyderabad officially became a part of **India** on **17th September 1948**, which is now celebrated as **Hyderabad Liberation Day**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Operation Shield**__

 __
 
• This name does not correspond to any specific historical operation related to the annexation of Hyderabad or the Indian independence movement.
 
• The term may refer to hypothetical or fictional operations in other contexts but is not relevant to the integration of Hyderabad.
 
 
 
• **Operation Peace**__
 __
 
• This term is generic and does not denote any specific historical event in Indian history.
 
• It may refer to peacekeeping missions or initiatives in other contexts but not to the integration of Hyderabad.
 
 
 
• **Operation Lotus**__
 
 
• The term **Operation Lotus** is associated with political strategies in modern Indian politics.
 
• It is unrelated to the historical context of Hyderabad's annexation in 1948.
